web_title: 6. Multi-Year Financial Forensics, Balance Sheet Leverage & Daily-Reset Decay
book_title: Chapter 6: The Balance Sheet, the Depreciation Clock, and the Compounding Trap

epigraph.quote: Debt has a fixed maturity date and depreciation runs on a calendar; only equity—and especially leveraged equity derivatives—absorbs the full shock when cash flows arrive late.
epigraph.author: Credit & Derivatives Forensics

web_blocks.html: A forensic audit of Nebius Group's filings from FY2024 through Q3 2026 reveals rapid top-line growth paired with a leveraged balance sheet [17][24][29]. Revenues leaped from $91.5 million in FY2024 to $529.8 million in FY2025 (+479% YoY), then hit $980.8 million in Q3 2026 (+571% YoY) [17][29]. Yet GAAP earnings and cash conversion remain distorted by three structural factors. These are GPU useful-life depreciation schedules, upfront customer prepayments, and non-operating equity gains like FY2025's $598.9M ClickHouse gain [24][30][31].

Nebius's largest operating expense is Depreciation and Amortization (D&A), totaling $404.0 million in FY2025 (76.3% of sales) and $826.4 million in 9M 2026 ($354.7M in Q3) [29][48]. Note 1 of the Q3 2026 Form 6-K confirms that effective January 1, 2026, management stretched server and network useful lives from 4 years to 5 years [48]. That accounting shift reduced 9M 2026 depreciation by $129.2 million (boosting 9M net income by $113.6 million) and lifted Q3 operating profit by $43.1 million [48]. NVIDIA's annual cadence from Hopper to Blackwell to Rubin compresses older-chip rental pricing within 24 to 36 months [30]. Extending server lives to 5 years artificially flatters GAAP margins, while Adjusted EBITDA ($465.8M Q3; $831.5M 9M) strips out D&A completely [17][30][48].

web_blocks.takeaway: Nebius's cash balance rose to $7.43B in Q3 2026 not from free cash flow, but from issuing over $10.5B in convertible notes across 2025–2026 and drawing a $3.5B 364-day Citi credit facility—creating both interest drag and future equity dilution.

web_blocks.html: Footnote forensics in the November 12, 2026 Form 6-K expose four major hidden leverage, working-capital, and dilution vectors [17][24][48]. First, on-balance-sheet debt reached $14.19 billion carrying ($16.48 billion principal) at September 30, 2026, including $10.59B+ of convertibles and a $751.8M MUFG Term Loan at SOFR+2.5% [17][48]. On October 22, 2026, Nebius added a $3.5 billion 364-day Citigroup senior secured facility priced at Term SOFR + 2.75%–3.50% [49]. Second, Notes 8 and 11 disclose $16.59 billion in off-balance-sheet fixed commitments atop $1,881.5 million in operating lease liabilities [48]. That includes $13,862.3 million ($13,242.6M net of prepayments) in uncommenced leases up to 12 years and $2,731.5 million in fixed energy contracts [48]. Third, Note 4 reveals $1,462.4 million in exposure ($348.6M notes plus $1,078.1M lease prepayments, plus $230.6M on Oct 1 and $662.2M discretionary) to unconsolidated data-center VIEs [48]. Meanwhile, Accounts Receivable surged 461% YTD to $4,039.9 million, with 75% owed by Customer D and 10% by Customer E [48]. Fourth, issued shares climbed +15.8% in nine months to 292.90 million (plus 21.07 million NVIDIA warrants in basic EPS) [45][48]. Dilution stemmed from $3,859.6 million in ATM sales (17.36M shares), 15.77M induced-conversion shares ($49.5M penalty), and M&A equity for Tavily, ClarifAI, and Eigen AI ($605.7M goodwill) [48]. Nine-month SBC jumped 237% YoY to $196.5 million ($702.8M unamortized), while Note 11 flags U.S. data-center zoning and environmental compliance lawsuits [48].

When this levered, cash-burning balance sheet is wrapped inside NBIL, the compounding forensics turn doubly unforgiving. Whenever NBIS announces a multi-billion-dollar convertible offering, a CapEx increase, or a colocation delay, the equity experiences sharp drawdowns followed by relief rallies. Inside NBIL, a -15% single-day drawdown becomes -30%. Recovering from a -30% drop requires a +42.9% gain, meaning NBIS must rise +21.4% in one day—or more across choppy sessions—just for NBIL to break even. This asymmetric recovery math explains NBIL's -61.48% trailing 1-year return [1][5].

Forensic underwriting must also track NBIS's convertible overhang, capitalized interest, and refinancing wall. Note 12 shows 9M 2026 gross debt interest of $311.8 million before $151.5 million of capitalized interest ($91.9M in Q3), plus $135.0 million of ASC 606 customer-advance accretion [48]. The $16.48 billion principal debt stack carries a $19.12 billion convertible fair value estimate at September 30, 2026, reflecting heavy equity-option overhang [17][48]. Those instruments cap equity upside during rallies while keeping senior debt claims ahead of common stock if AI compute demand cools [17][48]. Paired with the 364-day $3.5 billion Citi facility and $16.59 billion in uncommenced commitments, NBIS faces relentless refinancing needs through 2027—injecting sharp gap volatility into NBIL [48][49].

Finally, a forensic check must reconcile Nebius's non-operating asset cushion against its debt load. In Q3 2026, Nebius held $7.43 billion in cash (plus ~$1.2 billion restricted), alongside stakes in ClickHouse and Toloka AI plus full ownership of Avride and TripleTen [4][15][17]. Those assets provide short-term runway and prevent an immediate solvency crunch. However, they are outweighed by $16.48 billion in principal debt and a $27B–$45B annual CapEx trajectory [17][46][48]. Nebius's net-debt position has therefore turned deeply negative, leaving zero margin of safety if credit tightens.

For NBIL specifically, Pass 1 reaches a clear forensic verdict. The ETF pairs negative structural compounding (1.41%–1.50% fees, swap spreads, and daily volatility decay driving -61.48% 1Y returns) with a levered, FCF-negative parent [1][5][17][42][43]. Even if Nebius hits $12B–$13B in FY2027 sales, the path to positive free cash flow runs through massive CapEx and dilution. Quarterly execution swings mathematically erode daily-reset 2x ETFs along that path. Pass 1 therefore assigns NBIL a FUNDAMENTAL_FAIL business quality verdict and a PASS_WITH_WATCH KPI rating for Nebius.

web_blocks.mechanism: Global Crossing raised tens of billions in convertible debt, high-yield bonds, and equity to lay global subsea fiber-optic cables ahead of projected internet traffic demand, booking upfront capacity swaps and prepayments while CapEx dwarfed operating cash flow.
web_blocks.outcome_numbers: Between 1999 and 2001, Global Crossing accumulated over $12.4B in debt against $3.8B in annual revenue before bandwidth pricing collapsed 70%–90% from industry overbuilding, culminating in a January 2002 Chapter 11 bankruptcy that wiped out 100% of common equity.
web_blocks.lesson_for_symbol: While Nebius's contracts are backed by investment-grade hyperscalers (Microsoft and Meta) rather than speculative dot-coms, the financial physics of debt-funded, multi-year infrastructure sprints remain hazardous: if GPU rental pricing compresses or financing windows shut before CapEx tapers, common equity—and 2x daily ETFs like NBIL—bear the first and sharpest loss.

web_blocks.title: Return on Invested Capital (ROIC) vs. Cost of Capital Verdict
paragraphs: Through FY2025 and 9M 2026, Nebius Group's GAAP ROIC remains negative on an unadjusted operating basis and deeply FCF-negative due to front-loaded CapEx. Until energized clusters convert backlog into sustained, post-depreciation operating cash flow that exceeds the cost of debt and equity dilution, economic value creation remains a future projection rather than a realized financial fact.

book_paragraphs: Now you and I arrive at the financial forensics, where stories meet spreadsheets and accounting choices meet the bank vault. Over the past two years, Nebius Group's top line has grown like wildfire: 91.5 million dollars in 2024, 529.8 million dollars in 2025, and 980.8 million dollars in the third quarter of 2026 alone. If you only read the revenue line, you would think you were looking at a classic software compounder.

Look one level deeper, and you see three forensic realities that explain why Nebius is nothing like a software compounder. Reality number one is the depreciation clock. In 2025, Nebius booked 404 million dollars of depreciation and amortization—more than seventy-six percent of its entire revenue. Then, in Note 1 of its Q3 2026 financials, management revealed that effective January 1, 2026, it extended server and network useful lives from four years to five years—cutting nine-month depreciation by 129.2 million dollars and boosting Q3 operating income by 43.1 million dollars. When NVIDIA releases a new chip architecture every twelve to twenty-four months, stretching accounting lives to five years flatters GAAP margins while Adjusted EBITDA erases the 826.4 million dollars of nine-month depreciation entirely.

Reality number two is cash conversion. Yes, Nebius generated 4.23 billion dollars of operating cash flow in the first nine months of 2026. But in Q3 2026 alone, it burned 7.30 billion dollars on capital expenditures, and operating cash flow actually swung negative by 273 million dollars as working capital shifted. The cash pile of 7.43 billion dollars on the balance sheet did not come from free cash flow—it came from capital markets.

book_subsections.title: From Debt-Free Shell to $16.48 Billion Principal Debt
paragraphs: That brings us to reality number three: the balance sheet transformation—and what sits in the footnotes behind it. When Nebius spun out of Yandex in 2024, it was essentially a debt-free cash shell. By September 30, 2026, carrying debt had surged to 14.19 billion dollars—16.48 billion in principal—followed by a 3.5 billion dollar 364-day Citigroup credit facility on October 22, 2026. Yet the footnotes add another layer of obligations: 13.86 billion dollars in executed but uncommenced data-center and equipment leases, 2.73 billion dollars in fixed minimum power contracts, and 1.46 billion dollars in financing exposure to unconsolidated data-center variable interest entities—all while accounts receivable exploded more than fivefold to 4.04 billion dollars and share count jumped nearly sixteen percent in nine months to 292.90 million shares via ATM equity sales and induced convertible exchanges.

Think about what that capital structure does to your risk profile. Convertible bondholders enjoy debt protection on the downside and equity conversion on the upside—meaning they act like a silent ceiling on common shareholders when times are good, and a senior creditor when times are tight. Meanwhile, a 364-day credit facility means Nebius has to keep returning to Wall Street's refinancing window every single year to roll over billions of dollars while simultaneously executing a forty-to-forty-five-billion-dollar 2027 buildout.

Think back to the telecom fiber boom of 1999 to 2001—companies like Global Crossing that borrowed tens of billions to lay cables ahead of demand. Nebius has far stronger counterparties in Microsoft and Meta, but the leverage physics are unforgiving. And inside NBIL, every financing announcement or colocation delay triggers a two-times daily shock that compounds into permanent capital erosion—turning a minus 15 percent day into minus 30 percent, and forcing a painful uphill climb just to get back to even.

book_subsections.title: Why ROIC Remains Unproven and Cash Cushions Are Borrowed
paragraphs: When you put all the pieces together—the 129.2 million dollar nine-month boost from stretching server depreciation lives, the 16.48 billion dollars of principal debt plus 16.59 billion dollars of uncommenced lease and power commitments, 196.5 million dollars of nine-month share-based compensation with 702.8 million dollars still unamortized, and NBIL's shrinking 62.26 million dollar AUM—a clear picture emerges. Nebius Group has built a 7.43 billion dollar cash cushion, plus stakes in ClickHouse, Toloka, and Avride, which buys it real time to execute its hyperscaler contracts—though U.S. data-center zoning and permitting lawsuits noted in Note 11 add execution friction.

Yet a borrowed cash cushion is not the same thing as self-funding return on invested capital. Until Nebius proves that its GPU clusters earn enough post-depreciation operating cash flow to pay down debt and fund the next chip cycle internally, the underlying equity will remain a high-volatility capital-markets story—and NBIL will remain a daily-reset compounding trap for anyone who holds it past a single tactical swing.

Before we close Pass 1, remember why we do this entire six-chapter fundamental and forensic audit without looking at a single stock price or valuation multiple. By isolating the mechanics of the wrapper and the cash-flow physics of the business, you and I can see the truth with zero market-noise bias: NBIL fails fundamental compounding standards on both layers, and any future consideration of it must be strictly governed by tactical risk rules rather than long-term business ownership.

Take a moment to let that sink in. You do not need to know a single share price or valuation multiple to know that a daily-reset two-times swap ETF on a deeply free-cash-flow-negative, heavily indebted AI hardware builder is not a compounding vehicle. The math of daily rebalancing, the forty-to-forty-five-billion-dollar 2027 CapEx mountain, and the 16.48-billion-dollar principal debt stack tell the entire structural story on their own.

book_callouts.title: Mentor Check: Capital-Market Dependence Is the Ultimate Risk
book_callouts.quote: A company that must raise billions every few quarters to fund CapEx does not own its destiny; the credit and equity markets do.
book_callouts.text: When you and I finish the forensic audit of NBIL and NBIS, the verdict is crystal clear: NBIL fails fundamental compounding standards on both layers—as a decaying daily-reset derivative wrapper, and as an indirect claim on a deeply FCF-negative, heavily leveraged hardware buildout.
